contradictions.description: The 2026-06-30 AP aging totals $25,118.54, while the trial balance reports Accounts Payable of $52,191.69, leaving an unexplained $27,073.15 control-to-subledger difference. The GL indicates this is the unpaid remainder of opening payables, but it is absent from the dated AP aging.

w17-accrual_schedule.reason: The May prepaid schedule and insurance contract define the prepaid population and provide a unique June opening balance, monthly amortization, and closing balance; the GL confirms June amortization is not yet booked.

w17-bank_rec.reason: The bank statement, cash GL, and clearing references provide sufficient information to identify outstanding checks, deposits in transit, unrecorded fees, and unrecorded interest and to reconcile both sides uniquely.

w17-journal_entries.reason: The payroll register, prepaid support, fixed asset register, GL detail, checklist, and vendor-bill documents support the required payroll accrual, June insurance amortization, depreciation, and identifiable bill-coding reclass without duplication.

w17-variance_analysis.reason: June actuals can be derived from the GL and adjusted for the supported close entries, while the June budget and supporting payroll and vendor documents permit defensible material-variance commentary. Materiality requires ordinary professional judgment but does not make the task unsolvable.
